summary: assignment to object in conditional causes type error on function w/ record type return type

Comment 0 (2012-02-29): slightly dodgy code :) /** @returns {{prop1: (Object|undefined), prop2: (string|undefined), prop3: (string|undefined)}} */ function func(a, b) { var results; if (a) { results = {}; results.prop1 = {a: 3}; } if (b) { results = results || {}; results.prop2 = 'prop2'; } else { results = results || {}; results.prop3 = 'prop3'; } return results; } results in this error: JSC_TYPE_MISMATCH: inconsistent return type found : ({prop1: {a: number}}|{}) required: {prop1: (Object|null|undefined), prop2: (string|undefined), prop3: (string|undefined)} at line 18 character 7 return results; defining results on the first line on the function causes it the world. the still dodgy, but slightly less so, use of this is if the function return type were that record type|undefined and not all branches were guaranteed to be executed.
Comment 1 (2012-03-01): This issue was closed by revision r1802.
